title: Spengler holds off Paffett at Oschersleben
dek: Bruno Spengler won at Oschersleben from pole for BMW Team Schnitzer, 0.629 seconds ahead of Gary Paffett, and cut the championship deficit to 11 points with two races left.

chapters.title: Three title rivals, one Sunday
text: The eighth of ten rounds, on Sunday 16 September 2012, came three weeks after a Zandvoort race that had scrambled the table. Edoardo Mortara had won a wet-dry afternoon for Audi Sport Team Rosberg, ahead of Mike Rockenfeller and Mattias Ekström, and Gary Paffett had been spun around by Martin Tomczyk's BMW when the rain returned, recovering only to seventh. Even so Paffett still led the championship on 109 points, from Mercedes driver Jamie Green on 93 and Bruno Spengler on 91, so the gaps to the leader stood at 16 and 18 points.

Paffett arrived hoping that, barring incidents, the pace he had shown at Zandvoort would carry over. Green stressed that qualifying was especially important at Oschersleben. Spengler said he liked the place for its lack of long straights, its high kerbs and its mix of corners. BMW Team Schnitzer's principal Charly Lamm added that the way the new M3 DTM treated the kerbs would be central.

The weekend also carried a consequence from Zandvoort. Tomczyk, the reigning champion, had been given a five-place grid penalty for the contact with Paffett, to be served here. Behind the three title contenders, Mortara was fourth on 74 points, Tomczyk fifth on 69 and Rockenfeller sixth on 67, and Audi, after its one-two-three, hoped it might even be the front runner at Oschersleben.

chapters.title: Spengler sets the pace in the shoot-out
text: Qualifying was close all the way through. Spengler had a poor start to the session, still 18th with the chequered flag out in the first segment, before a last lap moved him through. He went on to be fourth fastest in the third segment, which made him the first of the four to run in the final shoot-out, and he put in 1:20.916. One by one Green, Paffett and Dirk Werner failed to beat it, and the pole was his, the third of his season.

Paffett took second, 0.086 seconds slower than Spengler at 1:21.002, so the top three of the championship started first, second and third on the grid, with Green on 1:21.226. Norbert Haug of Mercedes called it a showdown of the kind one could only dream about. Werner completed the second row for BMW Team Schnitzer on 1:21.911.

Ekström was the best of the Audi drivers in fifth, on 1:20.927. Tomczyk had qualified sixth on 1:20.999, but his five-place penalty dropped him to 11th on the grid, which moved Mortara up to sixth, with Rockenfeller seventh and Miguel Molina eighth. Farfus was ninth and Ralf Schumacher tenth, with Andy Priaulx 12th and Robert Wickens 13th. Joey Hand was 20th, the last of the BMWs, and the Persson Mercedes of Susie Wolff sat at the back.

chapters.title: Spengler holds the lead into the first corner
text: Spengler held first place from pole at the start, while Paffett had to fend off an attack from fellow Mercedes driver Green in the first corners. Green had briefly taken second place but was demoted again by the end of the first lap and ran third for the rest of the afternoon. The pair at the front then pulled clear of the field, with Spengler building a gap over Paffett in the opening stint.

The first corner was less kind to others. Priaulx, who had made a fine start and was running with Farfus and Tomczyk, was hit and pushed off there, and the damage to his splitter and side blunted his pace all afternoon; he was classified 17th, 12 laps down. Mortara, who had won at Zandvoort three weeks earlier, was out after only six laps, as was Rahel Frey, and David Coulthard's race lasted a single lap. Ekström made a poor start and lost ground.

chapters.title: An early stop for the leader
text: The stops did not change the order at the front. Spengler came in for his first tyre change before Paffett, and with fresh tyres he extended his lead while the Mercedes driver stayed out on worn rubber for several more laps. Paffett was unable to match his pace in that phase and later said the car had been very fast but that his team had lost too much time at the stops.

Behind them Farfus, who had made a good start and cleared the first corners cleanly, benefited from a pit-stop strategy that Bart Mampaey of the RBM team described as working well. Tomczyk had a short race. His RMG BMW began to run hot after about a third of the distance, and he retired after 20 laps, having already had a difficult weekend with the grid penalty. Wolff was also out, after 12 laps.

chapters.title: Paffett closes to 0.6 seconds
text: After the second stops the gap between the leaders tightened. Paffett, on used tyres, cut the gap over the closing kilometres, but he could not get close enough to attempt a pass. Spengler took the flag after 51 laps in 1:12:09.607, 0.629 seconds ahead. Green was third, 15.512 seconds behind the winner, and Werner was fourth.

Werner, 22.311 seconds back, scored the best result of his DTM career, and Farfus took fifth, 24.423 seconds behind, helped by that start. Rockenfeller finished sixth as the best Audi, ahead of Wickens in the Mücke Mercedes, with Ekström eighth, Albuquerque ninth and Scheider tenth. Hand just missed the points in 11th after climbing from 20th on the grid. Christian Vietoris was 12th ahead of Schumacher, Roberto Merhi and Molina, a lap down in 15th.

chapters.title: Spengler within 11 points with two races left
text: Spengler called it a great day for BMW and thanked his team for an unbelievable car. He said Paffett had put him under pressure at the end, that he could not afford a mistake, and that the early tyre change and long stints, helped by consistent tyres on the high kerbs, had been the key. Paffett said the race pace had been good but that Spengler was about as quick, and that on used tyres he had closed up a little, but not enough. Haug called an 11-point cushion not huge, but better than being 11 behind.

The table now read Paffett 127, Spengler 116, Green 108, Rockenfeller 75, Mortara 74 and Tomczyk 69. Spengler's third win had lifted him past Green into second, 11 points off the lead and eight clear of the Mercedes driver, and with 50 points available from the last two races he could still win the title without help from anyone else. Rockenfeller, now fourth, trailed Paffett by 52 points, and Audi's last hopes of a drivers' title had gone, a bitter contrast with the one-two-three three weeks before. Wolfgang Ullrich of Audi promised a stronger showing at Valencia and Hockenheim.

BMW had three cars in the top five, with Spengler, Werner and Farfus finishing first, fourth and fifth, and Jens Marquardt called it a sensational weekend. Werner said he was delighted with his best DTM result, though a podium had been just out of reach behind Green, while Farfus said the start had been the key and that a good set-up had come only in time for the race. Hand, up from 20th, said he would gladly take 11th after a difficult weekend, and Priaulx rued being hit on the first corner when the pace of the car had been good. Tomczyk, 58 points behind and therefore out of the title picture, said it simply had not been his weekend, with the penalty, a damaged car in practice and then the cooling trouble in the race.
The ninth round, at Valencia, follows on 30 September, with the season finale at the Hockenheimring on 21 October.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler led from pole to win the 51-lap race in 1:12:09.607, 0.629 seconds ahead of Gary Paffett, for his third victory of 2012.
